item.title: Conjoined twins head to Saudi Arabia for life-changing separation surgery
item.description: Ten-month-old conjoined twins Di Cecea and Jesipeli Kikau will leave Fiji tomorrow for Saudi Arabia, where they are scheduled to undergo a life-changing separation surgery. The Ministry of Health and Medical Services says the twins were born at the Colonial War Memorial Hospital in Suva alongside their singleton sister, Hossana.
item.content:encoded:
Ten-month-old conjoined twins Di Cecea and Jesipeli Kikau will leave Fiji tomorrow for Saudi Arabia, where they are scheduled to undergo a life-changing separation surgery.

The Ministry of Health and Medical Services says the twins were born at the Colonial War Memorial Hospital in Suva alongside their singleton sister, Hossana.

The ministry says the surgery will be carried out at King Salman Hospital in Saudi Arabia, with the Saudi Government fully funding the family’s airfares and accommodation as part of the strong bilateral relationship between Fiji and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

The Ministry of Health is covering the cost of a medical escort to accompany the family on their journey.

The ministry has called on Fijians to keep the family in their prayers, expressing hope for a successful operation and the safe return of the children to Fiji.

item.title: Volcanic ash reaches Fiji airspace, disrupting Fiji Airways flights

The airline says the ash cloud is affecting both Vanuatu and Fiji airspace, leading to the cancellation of flights to Port Vila and Funafuti, as well as several domestic services to Taveuni, Savus
item.content:encoded:
Volcanic ash from the ongoing eruption of the Manaro Voui volcano on Ambae Island in Vanuatu has spread into Fiji airspace, forcing Fiji Airways to cancel a number of regional and domestic flights today.

The airline says the ash cloud is affecting both Vanuatu and Fiji airspace, leading to the cancellation of flights to Port Vila and Funafuti, as well as several domestic services to Taveuni, Savusavu, Labasa and Cicia.

Fiji Airways says passenger safety remains its highest priority and operations will continue to be reviewed as the volcanic ash cloud moves across the region.

Affected passengers are being contacted directly and will be offered alternative travel arrangements where available.

The airline is also urging travellers to check the status of their flights regularly on the Fiji Airways website.

The disruptions follow the continued eruption of the Manaro Voui volcano, with Vanuatu’s Geological Hazards Department maintaining Alert Level 3.

item.title: Plans in place for major transformation
item.description: A NEW town square, relocated market and bus station, upgraded riverfront and stronger flood protection measures form part of a draft blueprint that will guide Navua’s future growth as part of its declaration as a town. This proposed scheme was outlined by senior Town Planner at the Department of Town and Country Planning Masilini Rokowati, during public consultations in Navua, describing it as a l
item.content:encoded:
A NEW town square, relocated market and bus station, upgraded riverfront and stronger flood protection measures form part of a draft blueprint that will guide Navua’s future growth as part of its declaration as a town.

This proposed scheme was outlined by senior Town Planner at the Department of Town and Country Planning Masilini Rokowati, during public consultations in Navua, describing it as a long-term framework that will shape development across the township.

“We want Navua to be a lively, connected and growing place,” she said.

She said the proposed town centre would support new commercial activity, including shops and businesses, while allowing for different types of housing, open spaces and parks.

Under the draft plan, Thompson Park has been identified as the proposed location for the relocated market and bus stand, with the area also expected to accommodate the town square with facilities such as a council office, library and bus station.

The existing market site along the riverfront is proposed to be redeveloped into a promenade, providing walking areas and open spaces for residents.

Ms Rokowati added that improved connectivity would also be a key focus, with Tokotoko, Calia and Naitata roads identified as important access routes into the town.

She said the proposed township would cover about 750 hectares and more than 1800 lots.

She noted that while Navua already has reliable water, electricity and transport networks, the planning study identified gaps in wastewater systems, stormwater management and the condition of the jetty in Naitonitoni that will require future investment.

Ms Rokowati explained the draft scheme also addresses flood and earthquake risks through hazard mitigation measures and improved land-use planning.

Residents were told the consultation marks only the first stage of the planning process, with further opportunities for public feedback before the scheme was finalised.

item.title: Navua nears town status
item.description: NAVUA could officially be declared a town as early as next month, says Minister for Housing and Local Government Maciu Nalumisa. Speaking in an interview after public consultations held in Navua, Mr Nalumisa said the process to declare Navua a town first started in 1973, but rapid economic growth and new developments have made the declaration more important than ever.
item.content:encoded:
NAVUA could officially be declared a town as early as next month, says Minister for Housing and Local Government Maciu Nalumisa.

Speaking in an interview after public consultations held in Navua, Mr Nalumisa said the process to declare Navua a town first started in 1973, but rapid economic growth and new developments have made the declaration more important than ever.

Mr Nalumisa said public consultations had received strong support from residents who have waited many years for the area to gain town status.

They have been longing for this for a very long time.”

He said town status would bring long-term benefits, including increased Government investment, improved infrastructure and greater opportunities to attract private investment.

He also confirmed that the Ministry is aiming to complete the declaration next month, although planning work and further consultations on the town planning scheme would continue.

He added that the two provinces linked to Navua, Serua and Namosi and their chiefs have given their support for the declaration to make Navua Fiji’s 14th town.

item.title: Defence lawyers request stay on civil proceedings
item.description: SEVERAL parties sued by former Supervisor of Elections Mohammed Saneem over an alleged unpaid leave entitlement of $54,443.71 have applied to stay the civil proceedings pending the outcome of the State’s appeal in the related criminal case. Lawyer Geraldine Naguilevu, representing the five defendants, confirmed before Justice Savenaca Banuve yesterday that the stay application was filed on July 23
item.content:encoded:
SEVERAL parties sued by former Supervisor of Elections Mohammed Saneem over an alleged unpaid leave entitlement of $54,443.71 have applied to stay the civil proceedings pending the outcome of the State’s appeal in the related criminal case.

Lawyer Geraldine Naguilevu, representing the five defendants, confirmed before Justice Savenaca Banuve yesterday that the stay application was filed on July 23.

The defendants are the President, the Prime Minister, the Constitutional Offices Commission, the Solicitor-General, and the Attorney-General.

Mr Saneem claims he is owed $54,443.71 in unpaid leave entitlements following his resignation. He said that after being suspended on full pay following the change of government after the 2022 General Election, he resigned and his resignation was accepted by the President the following year with immediate effect.

He claims he was entitled to a payout for 48 days of accrued annual leave and time-off in lieu, totalling $67,307, but received only $12,863.86. He argues the outstanding balance should have been paid under Section 136(1) of the Constitution.

The civil proceedings had been awaiting the outcome of the criminal case in which Mr Saneem and former attorney-general Aiyaz Sayed-Khaiyum were charged with receiving a corrupt benefit. Although both men were acquitted on June 26, the State has since appealed the acquittals.

Earlier this year, Justice Banuve ruled that the validity of the Deed of Variation was central to both the civil and criminal proceedings, making the outcome of the criminal case relevant to the civil claim.

The matter has been adjourned to August 14 for mention.

item.title: InsideSTORY I MSMEs: The backbone of the economy
item.description: MICRO, small and medium enterprise (MSMEs) are the backbone of the economy and play a vital role in the growth and development of the country. This was stated by the Fiji Revenue and Customs Service (FRCS) Taxation director Momina Begg at last week’s MSME Day Celebration 2026 in Suva, in which 252 micro, small and medium entrepreneurs from the FRCS MSME Business Community were recognised for their
item.content:encoded:
MICRO, small and medium enterprise (MSMEs) are the backbone of the economy and play a vital role in the growth and development of the country.

This was stated by the Fiji Revenue and Customs Service (FRCS) Taxation director Momina Begg at last week’s MSME Day Celebration 2026 in Suva, in which 252 micro, small and medium entrepreneurs from the FRCS MSME Business Community were recognised for their commitment to business development, tax compliance and continuous learning through a certificate presentation ceremony.

Ms Begg said MSME contributions in Fiji have been evident through the economy’s performance despite the challenges Fiji faces amid geopolitical tensions currently impacting the global economy.

She said through MSME contributions, the tax revenue has been increasing over the year as well.

“One of the things I think is visible out there is how the economy is going and has been mentioned,” Ms Begg said.

“There are challenging times for Fiji. However, if you look at the tax revenue, we are growing our revenue,” she said.

Ms Begg said so far, the FRCS has achieved more than its $3.37 billion forecasted figure.

However, she did not reveal the total revenue collected and stated that the revenue collection is still going on.

She said one of the contributing factors of this success is FRCS’ commitment to empowering MSMEs with their tax and compliance training which educates and provides entrepreneurs the opportunity to become tax compliant and to manage and expand their businesses.

She added that these trainings have helped businesses in proper and accurate bookkeeping, preparing financial statements, profit and loss and balance sheet of their business accounts.

Suva Market Vendors Association president Sakiusa Buraisarasau said MSMEs play a very important role in Fijis economy because starting small is the first step to achieving greater results.

“This is where everything starts before we come to the big ones, because that’s all where we start. And if we start it right, we’ll end it right,” Mr Buraisarasau said.

He said once the small businesses grow, they provide opportunities for others and contribute more to the economy depending on the type of business.

He added that the tax compliance trainings by the tax office have helped him and the other vendors to manage their business records, keep things on track and overcome their fears regarding tax compliance.

“What the concern was before was issues which have resolved at the market because people were not able to secure proper engagements on bookkeeping and all those,” he said.

“Before we come to tax, we need to keep records of what we’ve been saving. We know it now and can do it by ourselves,” he said.

Micro business owner Sisilia Seviua of Sevi Enterprises, which specialise in home-made assorted jams and tamarind chutney, said MSMEs are the heartbeat of the economy.

“Because our little businesses make up to this whole dynamic of other businesses, without us, these big businesses and organisations will not function. That’s my opinion,” Ms Seviua said.

Among the 252 businesses that are part of the FRCS MSME Business Community, 39 entrepreneurs successfully completed a comprehensive three-year training and coaching program and graduated last week as independent business fully compliant with Fiji’s tax and customs requirements.

MSME entrepreneurs with their tax compliance certificates at the FRCS office in Suva last week. Picture: KARISHMA KUMARI

item.title: Lending platform to boost MSMEs
item.description: FIJI’S first ever peer-to-peer lending platform is on track for a prototype unveiling by the end of August. This was confirmed to this newspaper by local fintech ThirdRoc, who is developing the platform.
item.content:encoded:
FIJI’S first ever peer-to-peer lending platform is on track for a prototype unveiling by the end of August.

This was confirmed to this newspaper by local fintech ThirdRoc, who is developing the platform.

ThirdRoc country head Tawake Tuitokatuadua said while ThirdRoc is setting up the entity, the directorship and how the organisation will run and development work are also happening in the background.

“We are working with the Reserve Bank of Fiji and there are milestones we have to achieve to set this up, both in terms of the platform as well as the fintech organisation,” Mr Tuitokatuadua said.

“We are aiming towards end of August to have a prototype ready to showcase to other people,” he said.

He said the peer-to-peer lending platform will allow Micro Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) to access different types of financing solutions depending on the need of the businesses.

Mr Tuitokatuadua said the peer-to-peer lending platform is aimed to connect borrowers directly with investors through digital technology, creating an alternative funding channel outside the traditional banking system.

He added the platform will improve access to finance for MSMEs that struggle to secure conventional loans.

The platform is enabled by the Access to Business Funding Act 2025, drafted to improve access to finance for Fiji’s MSMEs and overseen and licensed by the Reserve Bank of Fiji.

item.title: Resort celebrates World Mangrove Day
item.description: DOUBLE Tree Resort by Hilton Fiji – Sonaisali Island brought together team members, resort guests and World Wildlife Fund (WWF) representatives for a morning of mangrove restoration, environmental education and conservation along the resort’s coastline to celebrate World Mangrove Day last Saturday (July 26). As part of continued partnership between the Hilton Global Foundation (HGF) and the WWF, a
item.content:encoded:
DOUBLE Tree Resort by Hilton Fiji – Sonaisali Island brought together team members, resort guests and World Wildlife Fund (WWF) representatives for a morning of mangrove restoration, environmental education and conservation along the resort’s coastline to celebrate World Mangrove Day last Saturday (July 26).

As part of continued partnership between the Hilton Global Foundation (HGF) and the WWF, about 15 participants joined the initiative, learning firsthand the vital role mangroves play in protecting Fiji’s fragile coastal ecosystems before helping prepare a site for mangrove restoration and then re-planting approximately 200 mangrove seedlings as part of the resort’s ongoing efforts to engage guests and team members in environmental and community initiatives.

“The activity coincides with the HGF’s recent commitment of $US5.4million ($F12.16) to 18 nonprofit organisations globally – its largest annual investment to date – supporting initiatives that expand career opportunities, strengthen community resilience and help make the world a better place to travel,” the resort said in a statement.

“As Hilton’s global philanthropic arm, HGF supports programmes aligned with Travel with Purpose, Hilton’s strategy to drive positive impact and create lasting value for its people, hotels, communities and guests.”

HGF, it added, is supporting WWF’s mangrove restoration programme in Fiji, where it is working with iTaukei (Indigenous Fijian) communities to restore eight hecatres of mangroves across two sites within the Great Sea Reef — the Ba River Estuary and the Yasawa Islands.

“This was a wonderful opportunity to bring our guests and team members together to learn more about Fiji’s incredible natural environment while making a meaningful contribution,” general manager DoubleTree Resort by Hilton Fiji Shanaka Perera said.

“As an island resort, we recognise the responsibility we have to help protect the ecosystems that make Fiji so unique.

“Through initiatives supported by Hilton Global Foundation and WWF’s conservation efforts in Fiji, we’re proud to provide opportunities for our guests and team members to engage with and learn more about protecting these important ecosystems.”

Mangroves are among the world’s most valuable coastal ecosystems, providing natural protection against storm surges and coastal erosion, improving water quality, storing significant amounts of carbon and creating essential nursery habitats for fish, crabs and marine life. In Fiji, they also play an important role in supporting local livelihoods, preserving cultural traditions and strengthening climate resilience for coastal communities.
